text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslavia's supreme defence council discussed the military and political situation in the region during its session on Tuesday.
- Federal parliament verified mandates of deputies in the chamber of citizens following Novemeber 3 federal elections. Opposition coalition Zajedno (Together) boycotted the session.
- Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini to visit Belgrade on Decemeber 12 on the invitation of Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic.
- Montenegrin parliament to hold its first session following November 3 elections on December 16.
- Thousands of people organise public protests throughout Serbia in support of opposition demonstrations held in Belgrade against alleged election fraud.

- Federal government set an import quota of 5,000 taxis for an unspecified period beginning in January. Customs duty reduced to just four percent from current 69 percent. -- Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
